summary: Phase4 does not introduce new credential storage or external execution paths; provider secrets remain handled by existing bridge save/test flows and model catalog requests are credential-free.
threat_model: Browser user can type API keys and model IDs in the LLM settings modal
Bridge provider status crosses from local bridge to FastAPI proxy to browser
Model catalog payloads are untrusted display data from local registry/models.dev cache
A malicious or oversized model name should not execute code because Vue escapes interpolated text

checks.evidence: server.test provider upsert response does not contain fake key or apiKey
getProviderModels performs GET /providers/{id}/models without API key payload
Model cache uses component-local Map/Set state; no localStorage cache added
appforge/web.py CSP and same-origin proxy path were not weakened

secrets_scan: No committed provider secret was introduced by Phase4 changes; fake test key remains constructed as test data and existing test asserts it is not echoed.
dependency_audit: No new dependency was added. ModelSelect uses Vue and TypeScript only.
residual_risks: Live provider calls still depend on user-supplied credentials and provider-side access controls.
Large provider catalogs can still be loaded on demand, so users with very constrained browsers may see heavy advanced-mode interactions after choosing to expand.
